name: Distance, speed, velocity, acceleration and motion graphs

terms.definition: How far an object moves; a scalar.
Distance travelled ÷ time: s = v t.
terms.examiner: Typical speeds: walking 1.5 m/s, running 3 m/s, cycling 6 m/s.
An object moving in a circle at constant speed has a changing velocity.

terms.definition: Change in velocity ÷ time taken: a = Δv / t.
terms.examiner: Units m/s². Deceleration is negative acceleration.
Higher tier: draw a tangent for the speed at a point on a curve.

terms.definition: Gradient gives acceleration; area under the graph gives distance travelled.
Near the Earth's surface, acceleration due to gravity is about 9.8 m/s².
terms.examiner: Terminal velocity is reached when air resistance equals weight.
